text:
Logan Mailloux didn't play his first game of the season until Nov. 10, after opening the year on injured reserve and a conditioning stint in Springfield. Seven games later he might be the most interesting defenseman in St. Louis. He has 8 points, including three-point nights in the 8-6 win over Anaheim and the 9-6 win over New Jersey, and the Blues have handed him 19:22 a night (up from 16:46 last season) and a real power-play role: he's been on the ice for 40% of their power-play chances, against 7% a year ago.

This is earned, not just lucky. His own chances are up, 0.72 expected goals per 60 minutes against 0.19 last season, and the Blues have controlled 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five. It is also seven games, high-scoring ones at that. Our numbers put his scoring talent nearer 1.1 points per 60 than the 3.5 he's producing, and Evolving-Hockey rated his last season below replacement level. The ice time is the signal to trust, because it settles faster than scoring. Watch whether he keeps the power-play job.
headline: Logan Mailloux's late start has turned into a breakout
